papers_read.title_as_printed: A Graph Gaussian Embedding Method for Predicting Alzheimer's Disease Progression with MEG Brain Networks (Xu et al., IEEE Trans Biomed Eng 2021;68(5):1579-1588, author manuscript)
A tensor decomposition scheme for EEG-based diagnosis of mild cognitive impairment (Faghfouri et al., Heliyon 10 (2024) e26365)

what_each_reports.P-173: Resting-state alpha-band MEG networks from 53 NC and 76 MCI patients (Madrid), MCI split after ~3 years into sMCI (48) and pMCI (28); MG2G embeddings + 10 classifiers, 5-fold CV, mean accuracy 78% for sMCI/pMCI (79% NC/sMCI, 82% NC/pMCI, 61% 3-class). AUCs are shown only in supplementary figures; the main text states no AUC value.
what_each_reports.P-153: EEG spectral tensors (5x5 electrode grid x 60 micro-band powers) with PARAFAC decomposition and RBF-SVM for MCI vs healthy detection. Dataset I (Isfahan Noor hospital, 61 subjects): mean accuracy 93.96% (sensitivity 96.07%, specificity 96.98%) over three random 41/20 subject splits; Dataset II (Emotiv, 40 subjects): 78.65%. No AUC and no conversion analysis.

quantity_a: Cross-validated discrimination of MEG network embeddings for sMCI vs pMCI (~3-year conversion to AD), Madrid MEG cohort (record cites an AUC present only in the supplement)
quantity_b: Mean accuracy over three random subject-level train/test splits for current MCI vs healthy detection from resting EEG, Isfahan dataset (61 subjects)
incompatible_if_same: No comparison arises: P-153's 93.96% is an MCI-vs-healthy detection accuracy and P-173's contested figure is a conversion AUC; different contrast and different metric type.

gates.task: mismatch: P-153 is current MCI vs healthy detection (T1), not conversion; P-173's contested figure is sMCI vs pMCI (T2). The record's 'Acc 93.96 on T2' and task_equal='Yes' are wrong; no waiver on record
gates.dataset_family: mismatch: Madrid San Carlos MEG cohort vs the Isfahan EEG dataset (and an Emotiv dataset); the record's dataset_equal='Yes' is wrong
gates.validation_tier: match: both internal only (5-fold CV vs three random subject splits)
gates.modality_family: match at family level: resting-state electrophysiology (MEG vs EEG)

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible: different endpoint (3-year conversion vs current MCI status) and different metric types (AUC vs accuracy)
performance_validity: flag does not apply: P-153's 93.96% is below 0.97 (one split reached 96.52%); it is not a performance comparison on a shared quantity in any case
independence: Independent: different groups and cohorts; no shared authors.
grounds: The record misreads P-153's task: it classifies MCI against healthy subjects and contains no conversion analysis, so 'on T2' is wrong.
A detection accuracy set against a conversion AUC describes no disagreement; the metric types also differ.
The task and dataset-family gates fail with no waiver on record (Madrid MEG conversion cohort vs Isfahan EEG detection dataset).
P-173's main text reports only accuracies and places AUCs in the supplement, so the record's 'AUC 0.81' is not verifiable from the extract.

evidence_quotes.quote: MG2G achieved high performance with 61% for NC/sMCI/pMCI classification, 79% for NC/sMCI classification, 78% for sMCI/pMCI classification, and 82% for NC/pMCI classification.
Receiver operating characteristic area-under-the-curve (AUC) plots are shown in Suppl. Figs. 1 and 2.
Then, using parallel factor analysis (PARAFAC) tensor decomposition, the features are extracted, and a support vector machine (SVM) is used to discriminate MCI from normal subjects.

The results showed that the tensor-based method outperformed conventional methods in diagnosing MCI with an average classification accuracy of 93.96% and 78.65% for the first and second datasets, respectively.
The dataset includes 61 people over the age of 55,29 of them had MCI, and 32 of them were healthy.

record_defects: claim_b 'P-153: Acc 93.96 on T2' is wrong on task: P-153 is MCI vs healthy detection (T1); its own registry row codes T1.
task_equal='Yes' and dataset_equal='Yes' are wrong (conversion vs detection; Madrid MEG vs Isfahan EEG).
claim_a 'P-173: AUC 0.81' is not stated in the main text of the P-173 extract.
P-153 registry Method_Architecture holds abstract spillover text; its Dataset 'not reported' is wrong (the paper names the Isfahan Noor hospital dataset of Ref. [24] and an Emotiv dataset).
The 'bridging evidence' list names no condition separating the two results.
what_would_change_the_verdict: Nothing in these two papers: P-153 has no conversion result. A genuine candidate would need another MEG/EEG sMCI-vs-pMCI study over a comparable horizon with an AUC whose interval excludes P-173's.
